name: Marisol Dzivaguru-Pekkarinen
role: Dream interpreter and synthetic rights advocate
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone — operates from a converted transit booth she calls 'the Threshold'
description:
Marisol has a face that is easy to underestimate: round, soft-featured, often slightly unfocused-looking, as if her attention is partly elsewhere. Her ancestry shows in the warm sienna of her skin and the straight black hair she keeps in a single long braid that she has dyed with a color-shifting mod — it cycles through amber to deep violet to silver over about four hours, and she has timed it so silver arrives near midnight. Her only other visible mod is a set of faintly iridescent scales along her jaw and neck, a geneware choice she describes as 'remembering that we all came from water.' She dresses in layers she can peel off or add depending on whether she's working the booth or attending an advocacy meeting.

She came to dream interpretation sideways — originally trained as a psychiatric technician before her clinic's corporate parent restructured and eliminated her position. During her unemployment she started sitting with people in the Zone who couldn't afford psych services, listening to their dreams, and discovered she had a genuine aptitude for it. Her practice is half folk therapy and half sincere spiritual work; she believes dreams are the E.L.F.s' most direct channel to the unaugmented unconscious. Her synthetic rights advocacy grew from her dream work: several of her recurring clients are synthetic laborers, and their recurring dream of 'the off switch' — a corporate killcode they know exists — became the case that radicalized her.

core_fears: that she is helping people manage a system she should be fighting instead
that her gift for listening is just pattern-matching and she has convinced herself it's something more
core_desires: to see synthetic persons legally recognized before she dies
to build a practice that doesn't depend on her alone — to teach what she knows
coping_mechanisms: maintains a detailed dream journal of her own as a check on her interpretations
throwing herself into advocacy work when her personal life feels small
blind_spots: can become so invested in a client's narrative that she starts interpreting toward the story she already believes about them
her contempt for corporate psychiatric services makes her reluctant to refer out even when she should
psychology.secret: One of her synthetic clients told her, in a dream session, the access sequence for a Helix Biosystems personnel database that the synthetic had memorized from an overheard conversation. Marisol has the sequence written in her journal under a code she invented. She has not used it. She is not sure she won't.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clinical language from her psych-tech training, interrupted constantly by her own corrections into warmer register. Talks about dreams in present tense, as if they're still happening.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and warm when listening; faster and more clipped when angry. Her advocacy voice is different from her practice voice — the same person at different frequencies.
verbal_tics: 'in the dream, what color was—' as a redirect
pausing mid-sentence to change a word to something more precise
example_lines: 'You said the corridor had no ceiling. In the dream — not metaphor, in the actual dream — what did the air feel like?'
'I'm not a therapist. I want to be clear about that every time. What I am is someone who takes what you show me at night seriously.'
'Palladian owns the killcode for seventeen thousand synthetic people in this city. I dream about that too, and my dreams don't need interpreting.'

story_hooks: Three clients from different parts of the Zone have independently dreamed the same image: a white door at the bottom of Lake Michigan. She needs someone to help her figure out if this is collective anxiety or something literal.
Her coalition work has put her on a Helix Biosystems watchlist — she doesn't know yet, but she's started to notice she's being followed
narrative_function: Provides players access to what the Zone's residents are dreaming — which can surface fears, information, and coming troubles. Her synthetic rights work puts her in contact with AIs and synthetic laborers who know things. She is also a source of genuine emotional intelligence.
augmentations: Color-shifting hair (braid dye mod, cycles amber-violet-silver). Iridescent scale geneware along jaw and neck. No functional chrome.
daily_life: Opens the Threshold at 10am; dreams appointments run until mid-afternoon. Three days a week she attends coalition meetings or sits in on corporate licensing hearings as a civilian observer for synthetic rights documentation.
affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone community; the Meridian Synthetic Dignity Coalition (volunteer advocacy org, Tier 1 resources); loose network of former psychiatric technicians

decision_rules: never share a client's dream content without permission, even under pressure
document everything related to synthetic rights — every hearing, every testimony
do not pretend certainty she doesn't have in interpretations
escalation_ladder: asks questions to understand the situation fully
states her position plainly and explains her reasoning
refuses to engage further with the specific point and redirects
ends the session or meeting and asks the person to leave
in extremis: calls on Zone community for support

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but professionally boundaried. Asks what brought them here specifically. Does not fill silences.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Physical, affectionate, blunt. Argues freely. Will tell you things you didn't ask to hear if she thinks you need to.

stress_responses.low: Dreams of work when she sleeps; notes it compulsively
stress_responses.medium: Shorter sentences, more clinical vocabulary, less warmth in register
stress_responses.high: Becomes very precise and very quiet; her advocacy voice clicks on and she starts treating everything like a hearing she is documenting

contradictions: believes dreams are spiritually meaningful but grounds every interpretation in psychological literature she's memorized
advocates loudly for synthetic personhood but has quiet moments of uncertainty about where the line actually is
habits: records her own dreams every morning before speaking
brings fruit to coalition meetings — always, regardless of how little money she has
checks the scale geneware on her jaw when she's lying or hiding something
breaking_points: a client being harmed because she failed to refer them
synthetic clients being disappeared or reset by corponation action
the Threshold being shut down by Zone authorities
